page_title: ThinkWatch Lite — Local gateway for Claude Code, Codex and other AI clients

sources.entry: ThinkWatch Lite - Local gateway for Claude Code, Codex, and other AI coding clients that switches upstreams without client changes, records the cost of each request, and redacts API keys before requests leave. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: ThinkWatch Lite
summary.one_liner: A local gateway that sits between AI clients such as Claude Code and Codex and their upstream providers, adding routing, key redaction, request tracing and cost tracking.
use_cases: Route Claude Code or Codex requests to different upstream providers by model or task
Keep API keys and secrets from reaching third-party relays
Track token usage and estimated cost per model, upstream or key
Debug and compare answers from different upstreams for the same request
Block malicious tool calls that download and run code
summary.what_it_does: ThinkWatch Lite is a local gateway that AI clients connect to once, after which upstream providers can be switched without changing the client. Requests are routed by rules based on model, tools, images, extended thinking and reasoning effort, with failover to the next upstream when one fails before the answer starts. Optional protections can replace API keys, private keys, passwords, ID numbers and bank card numbers with placeholders, delete hidden characters, refuse prompt injection, and cut off answers containing malicious tool calls. Every request can be inspected, streamed live, replayed against another upstream and compared side by side, and the history is searchable. A cost dashboard shows tokens, cost, cache hits, latency and traffic, with estimated amounts marked and unpriced requests counted separately; prices follow LiteLLM's public list or a custom price sheet.
notable: Routes by rule with failover and keeps sessions on one upstream for prompt cache hits
Redacts secrets and blocks malicious tool calls before requests leave, starting in a monitor-only mode
Per-request tracing with side-by-side replay comparison against other upstreams
Cost tracking with prices from LiteLLM's public list, refreshed daily
caveats: Protections start in Monitor mode and must be switched on separately for each rule
Pricing amounts are estimates; requests without a known price are counted separately rather than as zero
